# Judith Chapter 11 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 11 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_011_page_001.jpg

---

**1** And Holofernes said to her, "Take courage, woman, and do not be afraid in your heart, for I have never harmed anyone who has chosen to serve Nebuchadnezzar, the king of all the earth.

**2** And now, if your people who dwell in the hill country had not despised me, I would not have lifted my spear against them; but they themselves have done these things to themselves.

**3** And now tell me, why did you flee from them and come to us? For you have come for safety. Take courage — you will live tonight and hereafter.

**4** For no one will harm you, but all will treat you well, as they do with the servants of my lord King Nebuchadnezzar."

**5** And Judith said to him, "Receive the words of your servant, and let your handmaid speak in your presence, and I will speak no falsehood to my lord tonight.

**6** And if you follow the words of your handmaid, God will bring to completion through you a perfect deed, and my lord will not fail in his purposes.

**7** As Nebuchadnezzar the king of all the earth lives, and as his power lives, who sent you for the setting right of every living soul — not only do men serve him through you, but also the beasts of the field and the cattle and the birds of heaven will live through your strength under Nebuchadnezzar and all his house.

**8** For we have heard of your wisdom and the clever devices of your soul, and it has been reported throughout all the earth that you alone are good in all the kingdom, mighty in knowledge, and wondrous in the arts of war.

**9** And now as for the word which Achior spoke in your council, we have heard his words; for the men of Bethulia rescued him, and he told them all the things he had said to you.

**10** Therefore, O master and lord, do not disregard his word, but lay it up in your heart, for it is true: for our people is not punished, nor does the sword prevail against them, unless they sin against their God.

**11** And now, so that my lord will not come up empty-handed and fail, death has also fallen upon them, and sin has seized them, with which they will provoke their God to anger whenever they do wickedness.

**12** Since their food ran out and all their water became scarce, they resolved to lay hands upon their cattle, and they determined to consume all the things which God by his laws had commanded them not to eat.

**13** The firstfruits of the grain and the tithes of the wine and oil, which they had consecrated and set aside for the priests who stand before the face of our God in Jerusalem — things which it is not lawful for any of the people even to touch with their hands —

**14** they have decided to consume these, and they have sent men to Jerusalem, because those dwelling there have also done this, to bring them permission from the council of elders.

**15** And it will be, when the word comes back to them and they do it, they will be given over to destruction on that same day.

**16** Therefore I your servant, knowing all this, fled from them, and God sent me to do with you things that will astound all the earth — as many as will hear about them.

**17** For your servant is devout, and serving the God of heaven day and night; therefore I will remain with you, my lord, and your servant will go out by night into the valley, and I will pray to God, and he will tell me when they have committed their transgressions.

**18** And I will come and tell you, and you will go out with your whole army, and not one of them will withstand you.

**19** And I will lead you through the midst of Judea until you come to Jerusalem, and I will set your throne in the midst of it; and you will drive them like sheep that have no shepherd, and not a dog will open its mouth before you. For these things have been told to me according to my foreknowledge, and were announced to me, and I was sent to tell you."

**20** And her words pleased Holofernes and all his servants, and they marveled at her wisdom and said,

**21** "There is no such woman from one end of the earth to the other, so fair in face and so wise in words."

**22** And Holofernes said to her, "God has done well to send you before the people, that power should be in our hands, and destruction among those who have despised my lord.

**23** And now you are beautiful in your face and you are good in your words; if you do as you have said, your God shall be my God, and you yourself shall dwell in the house of King Nebuchadnezzar and shall be renowned throughout all the earth."

---
*EMET renders Greek literally. "Set aside" renders aphorismena. "Firstfruits" renders aparchas. Judith's speech is technically truth in every clause — she is giving a layered, theologically sophisticated deception.*
